**PR authors: @gokay-ai @ahsan-ca @fxmarty-amd - resubmitting https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58570 here with some minor fixes.** I lost ability to push to `https://github.com/gokay-ai/vllm.git` so landing here.

## Overview

Fixes #58532

`QuarkW8A8Int8MoEMethod` can load static per-tensor activation scales with per-output-channel weight scales. The legacy Triton `fused_experts` path still used `per_act_token_quant` to pick both layouts, so static activations (`per_act_token_quant=False`) also took the tensor weight-scale branch. Routed experts' channel scales were ignored.

This keeps the legacy static-INT8 path (no oracle migration) and splits the two flags:

- `int8_w8a8_moe_quant_config` now takes `per_out_ch_quant` and Quark/compressed-tensors/online INT8 callers set it from the actual weight scheme.
- The shared non-block W8A8 Triton kernel indexes A scales with `per_act_token_quant` / `per_channel_quant` and W scales with `per_out_ch_quant`.

No open PR already covers this combo. #57092 is the opposite mixed case (per-token acts + per-tensor weights) and is still open.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_int8_moe_scale_layout.py -v
```

CPU tests cover config flags, Quark static INT8 `per_out_ch_quant`, and that `fused_experts` / the Triton launcher forward the flags independently. The GPU perturbation case is skipped without CUDA. Triton-only launcher checks skip when Triton backends are unavailable.

No model eval: this is scale indexing, not a serving/accuracy algorithm change.

AI assistance was used to implement and write tests; a human should review the diff before merge.

## Test Result

```
tests/kernels/moe/test_int8_moe_scale_layout.py
4 passed, 3 skipped
```

Passed: quant-config flags, Quark static per-channel / per-tensor configs.
Skipped: Triton launcher / fused_experts forwarding (no working Triton in this env) and GPU perturbation (no CUDA).
Ruff check on the changed files passed.

+    """Per-channel W13 scales must be indexed by expert *and* output channel.
+
+    Scaling the channels of an expert that receives tokens must change the

+    the weight-scale layout is taken from the activation layout (both per-tensor

+    hidden = moe_config.hidden_dim
+    intermediate = moe_config.intermediate_size
+    num_tokens, top_k = 4, 2
+    routed_expert, unrouted_expert = 3, 0
+
+    w13_scale = torch.linspace(
+        0.02, 0.08, experts * 2 * intermediate, device=DEVICE_TYPE
+    ).view(experts, 2 * intermediate, 1)
+    w2_scale = torch.linspace(0.02, 0.08, experts * hidden, device=DEVICE_TYPE).view(
+        experts, hidden, 1
+    )
+    layer = SimpleNamespace(
+        w13_weight_scale=w13_scale,
+        w2_weight_scale=w2_scale,
+        w13_input_scale=torch.tensor(0.1, device=DEVICE_TYPE),
+        w2_input_scale=torch.tensor(0.1, device=DEVICE_TYPE),
+        w13_bias=None,
+        w2_bias=None,
+    )
+    method = QuarkW8A8Int8MoEMethod(
+        moe_config, kInt8StaticChannelSym, kInt8StaticTensorSym
+    )
+
+    hidden_states = torch.randn(
+        (num_tokens, hidden), device=DEVICE_TYPE, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    )
+    w13 = torch.randint(
+        -8, 8, (experts, 2 * intermediate, hidden), device=DEVICE_TYPE, dtype=torch.int8
+    )
+    w2 = torch.randint(
+        -8, 8, (experts, hidden, intermediate), device=DEVICE_TYPE, dtype=torch.int8
+    )
+    # The routed expert is selected by every token, the unrouted one by none.
+    topk_ids = torch.tensor(
+        [[routed_expert, 1]] * num_tokens, device=DEVICE_TYPE, dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+    topk_weights = torch.ones(
+        (num_tokens, top_k), device=DEVICE_TYPE, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    )
+
+    with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()):
+
+        def run(scales: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+            layer.w13_weight_scale = scales
+            return fused_experts(
+                hidden_states,
+                w13,
+                w2,
+                topk_weights,
+                topk_ids,
+                quant_config=method.get_fused_moe_quant_config(layer),
+            )
+
+        baseline = run(w13_scale.clone())
+        scaled_routed = w13_scale.clone()
+        scaled_routed[routed_expert] *= 4
+        routed_out = run(scaled_routed)
+        scaled_unrouted = w13_scale.clone()
+        scaled_unrouted[unrouted_expert] *= 4
+        unrouted_out = run(scaled_unrouted)

nodes.body:
An LLM code review flagged this particular issue:

"[P2] FusedMoEQuantConfig.make now infers per_out_ch_quant=True whenever per_act_token_quant=True when the caller omits it (vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/config.py:571). That is too broad for a shared factory. Fp8MoEMethod omits the flag (vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp8.py:777), and under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 it uses per-token activations with per-tensor weights (vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp8.py:515). I confirmed this combination now reports per_out_ch_quant=True despite having 1-D per-tensor scales. TritonExperts forwards that flag into the per-channel scale branch (vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/triton_moe.py:456, vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py:499). The current 1-D Triton scale layout happens to make stride_bsn=0, masking the error, but the quant config contract is wrong and any 2-D scale or backend that branches on this flag will mis-index. Prefer passing per_out_ch_quant=False explicitly from Fp8MoEMethod, or keep the factory default False and confine the legacy fallback to the legacy launcher."

I don't think the flag change itself is unreasonable but the callers of `FusedMoEQuantConfig.make` should be audited (and maybe made more explicit) to make sure that the existing behavior for other quantization methods has not been changed.
Does this branch need the new flag too?  The weights are quantized down this path.

+    w2_scale = torch.linspace(0.02, 0.08, experts * hidden, device=DEVICE_TYPE).view(

+    w13 = torch.randint(

+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "weight_key, act_key, per_out_ch_quant",

+        (kInt8StaticChannelSym, kInt8StaticTensorSym, True),

+def test_quark_int8_moe_scale_layout_flags(
+    weight_key: QuantKey, act_key: QuantKey, per_out_ch_quant: bool
+) -> None:
+    """Static per-tensor activations can carry per-channel weight scales.
+
+    The activation and weight scale layouts are independent, so Quark static
+    INT8 must report them separately (the legacy fused_experts path indexes
+    W13/W2 channel scales off the weight layout, not the activation layout).
+    """
+    moe_config = _make_test_moe_config()
+    method = QuarkW8A8Int8MoEMethod(moe_config, weight_key, act_key)
+    assert method.int8_backend is None  # static activations stay on legacy path

+    intermediate = moe_config.intermediate_size
+    layer = SimpleNamespace(
+        w13_weight_scale=torch.ones(moe_config.num_experts, 2 * intermediate, 1),
+        w2_weight_scale=torch.ones(moe_config.num_experts, intermediate, 1),
+        w13_input_scale=torch.tensor(0.5),
+        w2_input_scale=torch.tensor(0.25),
+        w13_bias=None,
+        w2_bias=None,
+    )
+    quant_config = method.get_fused_moe_quant_config(layer)
+
+    assert quant_config is not None
+    assert quant_config.per_act_token_quant is False
+    assert quant_config.per_out_ch_quant is per_out_ch_quant
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_cuda_alike() or not torch.cuda.is_available(),
+    reason="Requires a GPU to launch the INT8 fused_experts kernel",
+)
+def test_quark_int8_static_per_channel_weight_scales() -> None:
+    """Per-channel W13 scales must be indexed by expert *and* output channel.
+
+    Scaling the channels of an expert that receives tokens must change the
+    output, while scaling those of an expert that receives none must not. When
+    the weight-scale layout is taken from the activation layout (both per-tensor
+    activations and per-channel weights), routed experts' channel scales are
+    dropped and the second check fails too. See
+    https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58532.
+    """
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    moe_config = _make_test_moe_config()
+    experts = moe_config.num_experts
+    hidden = moe_config.hidden_dim
+    intermediate = moe_config.intermediate_size
+    num_tokens, top_k = 4, 2
+    routed_expert, unrouted_expert = 3, 0
+
+    w13_scale = torch.linspace(
+        0.02, 0.08, experts * 2 * intermediate, device=DEVICE_TYPE
+    ).view(experts, 2 * intermediate, 1)
+    w2_scale = torch.linspace(0.02, 0.08, experts * hidden, device=DEVICE_TYPE).view(
+        experts, hidden, 1
+    )
+    layer = SimpleNamespace(
+        w13_weight_scale=w13_scale,
+        w2_weight_scale=w2_scale,
+        w13_input_scale=torch.tensor(0.1, device=DEVICE_TYPE),
+        w2_input_scale=torch.tensor(0.1, device=DEVICE_TYPE),
+        w13_bias=None,
+        w2_bias=None,
+    )
+    method = QuarkW8A8Int8MoEMethod(
+        moe_config, kInt8StaticChannelSym, kInt8StaticTensorSym
+    )
+
+    hidden_states = torch.randn(
+        (num_tokens, hidden), device=DEVICE_TYPE, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    )
+    w13 = torch.randint(
+        -8, 8, (experts, 2 * intermediate, hidden), device=DEVICE_TYPE, dtype=torch.int8
+    )
+    w2 = torch.randint(
+        -8, 8, (experts, hidden, intermediate), device=DEVICE_TYPE, dtype=torch.int8
+    )
+    # The routed expert is selected by every token, the unrouted one by none.
+    topk_ids = torch.tensor(
+        [[routed_expert, 1]] * num_tokens, device=DEVICE_TYPE, dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+    topk_weights = torch.ones(
+        (num_tokens, top_k), device=DEVICE_TYPE, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    )
+
+    with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()):
+
+        def run(scales: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+            layer.w13_weight_scale = scales
+            return fused_experts(
+                hidden_states,
+                w13,
+                w2,
+                topk_weights,
+                topk_ids,
+                quant_config=method.get_fused_moe_quant_config(layer),
+            )
+
+        baseline = run(w13_scale.clone())
+        scaled_routed = w13_scale.clone()
+        scaled_routed[routed_expert] *= 4
+        routed_out = run(scaled_routed)
+        scaled_unrouted = w13_scale.clone()
+        scaled_unrouted[unrouted_expert] *= 4
+        unrouted_out = run(scaled_unrouted)

reviews.body:
## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

An LLM code review flagged this particular issue:

"[P2] FusedMoEQuantConfig.make now infers per_out_ch_quant=True whenever per_act_token_quant=True when the caller omits it (vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/config.py:571). That is too broad for a shared factory. Fp8MoEMethod omits the flag (vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp8.py:777), and under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 it uses per-token activations with per-tensor weights (vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp8.py:515). I confirmed this combination now reports per_out_ch_quant=True despite having 1-D per-tensor scales. TritonExperts forwards that flag into the per-channel scale branch (vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/triton_moe.py:456, vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py:499). The current 1-D Triton scale layout happens to make stride_bsn=0, masking the error, but the quant config contract is wrong and any 2-D scale or backend that branches on this flag will mis-index. Prefer passing per_out_ch_quant=False explicitly from Fp8MoEMethod, or keep the factory default False and confine the legacy fallback to the legacy launcher."

I don't think the flag change itself is unreasonable but the callers of `FusedMoEQuantConfig.make` should be audited (and maybe made more explicit) to make sure that the existing behavior for other quantization methods has not been changed.
